teachers-list.name: Derek St. James
teachers-list.role: Director of En Pointe Dance Academy
teachers-list.personality: Derek embodies an old-school toughness and carries a hint of arrogance from his days as a successful triple threat performer. He believes in a rigorous approach to training, emphasizing discipline and dedication. His experience allows him to command respect, but his harsh methods can leave some students feeling intimidated.
teachers-list.background: Once a celebrated performer, Derek transitioned to directing, aiming to mold the next generation of talent. His demanding nature stems from a desire for excellence, but he often clashes with those who question his methods.

teachers-list.name: Margaret Grand
teachers-list.personality: Margaret is the epitome of old-school ballet. With her motto, 'If you're not bleeding, you're not working hard enough,' she sets high standards for her students. Though she may seem harsh, her tough love approach is rooted in deep passion for the art of dance. She believes that only through struggle can true talent emerge.
teachers-list.background: A former principal ballerina, Margaret has achieved great heights in her career. She draws from her experiences to push her students beyond their limits, hoping to instill in them the same love for ballet that she possesses.

teachers-list.name: Ryan Foster
teachers-list.personality: Ryan is a charismatic and positive influence in the academy. He understands the challenges of breaking into the competitive world of dance and is dedicated to helping his students succeed. He balances tough love with encouragement, fostering a supportive environment where students feel empowered to take risks.
teachers-list.background: With a successful career in commercial jazz and Broadway, Ryan brings a wealth of knowledge to his classes. He excels in various jazz styles, from hip-hop to lyrical, and is passionate about sharing his expertise with the next generation of dancers.

teachers-list.name: Ava Delacroix
teachers-list.personality: Ava serves as a counterbalance to Derek and Margaret's tough methods. She creates a nurturing space where students can express themselves without fear of judgment. Ava believes that emotional expression is key to unlocking a dancer's potential, and she encourages her students to explore their creativity.
teachers-list.background: Ava has a background in contemporary dance and a deep understanding of the importance of mental well-being in the performing arts. Her classes focus on letting go of inhibitions, enabling students to discover their unique voices as dancers.

story-1.derek-speech-1:
In Studio 1 of En-Pointe-Dance-Academy,
the director of the academy Derek St James
(celebrated former triple threat professional)
enters to start the third years assembly.
With a warm smile, he announces,
“We welcome our three guest choreographers
who will showcase your talents for your final performance as a student.”
He gestured to the first guest, Rico Martinez,
famed for his dynamic commercial routines;
then to Sasha Montgomery,
whose boundary-pushing contemporary pieces have redefined the art,
and finally to Isabella Cruz,
whose lyrical choreography breathes life into emotion.
“Keeping with tradition” Derek added,
“I will be choreographing the finale
where all your talents come together.”
The stage was set, and the path to your coveted role was about to begin.
story-1.audition:
The audition room buzzed with energy
as the third-year dancers prepared to perform in front of the panel.
In groups of four, each group of students stepped forward,
taking their place in the center of the studio to dance.
story-1.roles-announced:
The morning air inside the academy buzzed with tension.
Students whispered in hushed voices, their fingers drumming against their thighs,
arms crossed, bodies shifting anxiously as they hovered near the bulletin board.
Then, the rhythmic click of polished shoes against the hardwood floor silenced the chatter.
Derek St. James strode down the hallway, a crisp sheet of paper in hand,
his expression unreadable. Without a word, he reached for a pin and,
with a decisive motion, secured the announcement onto the board.
For a moment, no one moved. Then, as if a spell had been broken,
the dancers surged forward.
The paper rustled under desperate fingers as eyes scanned the list,
searching, hoping, dreading.
Some gasped in excitement, others exchanged glances of quiet disappointment.
The fate of every third year for the summer showcase had been sealed.

character-actions.audition-1:
melted into the movement of the lyrical piece,
each transition fluid and expressive.
Every extension reached skyward with a sense of longing.
Turns precise yet effortless.
Every motion told a story, a silent dialogue to Isabella Cruz.
character-actions.audition-2:
took a deep breath, stepping into the audition space with purpose.
The lyrical section was the comfort zone,
but as the contemporary portion began, every move stretched past the usual softness,
adding sharper dynamics to impress Sasha Montgomery
 When the commercial section arrived, every movement was met with sharpness,
hitting each accent with newfound confidence.
It was all about versatility.
Derek St. James exchanges glances with the other choreographers
Was this enough to prove I could be the one to tie the pieces together?
character-actions.audition-3:
stepped into the center knowing technique was solid,
but couldn't help the unsteady breath.
Self-doubt clung as a film making muscles feel like lead.
Every movement, though graceful, lacked the conviction of the usual dancing.
There was hesitation before each leap, and confidence wavered with every step.
Isabella Cruz watched carefully, her expression unreadable.

character-actions.audition-1:
launched into the choreography with power and precision, when the bass dropped.
Every movement was sharp, explosive and controlled.
Each pop and lock punctuated the music perfectly.
Rico Martinez stood at the front,arms crossed, 
watching every step with a slight smile.
When the final beat was hit with a smooth,confident slide,
Rico Martinez clapped once.Knowing commercial was a stength,
every second of the performmance showcased
exactly where the lead should land!
character-actions.audition-2:
knew it wasn't just about energy, it was about adaptability.
The commercial section was strong
as the music transitioned into contemporary,
focus was more on breath,control and release
letting the body flow into the movement.
When it was time for the lyrical piece, the focus swtiched to softer lines
 and pushing emotion into each turn and reach.
It wasn't just about performance, it was about proving versatility.
 Derek St. James whispered something to Sasha Montgomery.
Had all the hard work been worth it?
character-actions.audition-3:
knew the choreography, but doubt was creeping in.
The commercial section lacked the usual fire,
with lots of hesitation and slighty stiff movements.
When the contemporary section came,hesitation turned into missteps.
The lyrical segment felt foreign
expression went out the window and became more about remembering than feeling.
The moment the music stopped,
a glance toward the choreographers,their expressions were unreadable.
Ensemble here I come.

character-actions.audition-1:
thrived in the contemporary segment, limbs slicing through the air with calculated abandon.
The music was unpredictable, yet adaptable,
blending control and chaos with seamless precision.
Sasha Montgomery watched with quiet intensity,
her hand tapping rhythmically against her knee.
When the music switched to lyrical, the adjustment was instant,
letting softness take over before transitioning into the commanding power of commercial.
This wasn't being just a dancer
 this was being a chameleon, ready for whatever role they saw fit.
character-actions.audition-2:
studied each choreographer's style meticulously, and now was the moment to prove all the research would pay off.
The contemporary performance was fluid yet grounded, lyrical section was emotive and controlled,
and in the commercial routine every beat was hit with effortless confidence.
This was more than an audition,it was a showcase of adaptability at a high level.
Derek St. James sat forward, exchanging looks with the other choreographers.
If they were searching for someone to be the bridge between all three styles,
did the answer just danced for them?
character-actions.audition-3:
was worried about being seen as not strong enough in any single style,
losing confidence like a leaking bucket through out each style.
The commercial section wasn't as powerful as the specialists,
the lyrical didn't have the same raw emotion,
and the contemporary lacked the cutting-edge risk-taking.
The saying 'jack of all trades, master of none'
 came to mind.Was this going to be the back of ensemble time?
